follow_up_questions.question: Is the itching noticeably worse at night than during the daytime?
follow_up_questions.quoted_excerpt: it's itching a lot, like all the time. And I can't even sleep at night.
follow_up_questions.reasoning: Nocturnal predominance of itch strongly suggests scabies and is less typical of an atopic-dermatitis flare; clarifying the timing helps distinguish the provisional diagnosis from infestations or cholestatic pruritus.

follow_up_questions.question: What do the affected areas look like – dry red patches, tiny raised bumps, or fluid-filled blisters?
follow_up_questions.quoted_excerpt: would you say these symptoms are very similar to your eczema symptoms, or different?
follow_up_questions.reasoning: Precise lesion morphology differentiates atopic dermatitis (ill-defined dry erythematous patches) from urticaria (transient wheals), allergic contact dermatitis (vesicles), or scabies (papules/burrows), thereby increasing diagnostic accuracy.

follow_up_questions.question: Have you seen any yellow crusts forming on top of the cracked skin?
follow_up_questions.quoted_excerpt: My skin is a bit cracked in some parts, like kind of cracked, if you see what I mean.
follow_up_questions.reasoning: Yellow crusting suggests secondary impetiginisation of eczematous skin, guiding need for antibacterial therapy and helping rule out uncomplicated eczema flare.

follow_up_questions.question: Have you started using a new laundry detergent or fabric softener recently?
follow_up_questions.quoted_excerpt: So for example, have you changed your uh shower gel, any clothing? Have you been around anyone else?
follow_up_questions.reasoning: Contact allergens or irritants in washing products are common precipitants of acute widespread dermatitis; asking pinpoints an avoidable trigger and helps distinguish allergic contact dermatitis from atopic eczema.

follow_up_questions.question: Has any of your flatmates developed an itchy rash as well?
follow_up_questions.quoted_excerpt: I live with a few flatmates... I don't feel really comfortable asking about these questions.
follow_up_questions.reasoning: Person-to-person spread of itch strongly suggests scabies; absence of similar symptoms in co-habitants reduces the likelihood of infestation and supports the provisional eczema flare.

follow_up_questions.question: Do you have itching or spots between your fingers or around your wrists?
follow_up_questions.quoted_excerpt: Just the chest, hands and like, like inside the elbows. Yeah.
follow_up_questions.reasoning: Interdigital and wrist involvement is classic for scabies but less so for atopic dermatitis; clarifying distribution refines the differential.

follow_up_questions.question: Do the red itchy areas ever fade completely and then appear elsewhere within a few hours?
follow_up_questions.quoted_excerpt: Doctor: And apart from this, any other symptoms have you noticed? ... Patient: No. just very itchy. Nothing else.
follow_up_questions.reasoning: Transient, migratory lesions point toward acute urticaria, whereas persistent patches favor eczema or contact dermatitis, thereby sharpening diagnostic confidence.

follow_up_questions.question: Does anyone in your family have eczema, asthma, or hay fever?
follow_up_questions.quoted_excerpt: Patient: Uh, no. I just had asthma in the past. But not anymore.
follow_up_questions.reasoning: A personal or family atopic history supports atopic dermatitis and helps weigh it against other etiologies like contact dermatitis or scabies.

follow_up_questions.question: Have you been in close contact with any pets or animals over the last few weeks?
follow_up_questions.reasoning: Animal contact may introduce mites (e.g., scabies) or allergens provoking contact dermatitis; asking clarifies exposure risk and narrows differentials.
